reconstructed_theorem_text: Theorem: for every measurable space X, probability measure mu, fixed Gamma : (X -> R) -> (X -> R), fixed admissible : (X -> R) -> Prop, real C,l,u, and B : X -> R, assume C >= 0, B is mu-almost-everywhere measurable, l <= B mu-almost everywhere, B <= u mu-almost everywhere, and P(mu,Gamma,admissible,C). Put Z = integral_X exp(B(y)) dmu(y) and nu = mu.withDensity(x -> ofReal(exp(B(x))/Z)). Then P(nu,Gamma,admissible,C exp(u-l)). Ent_m(h) means integral_X h(x) log(h(x)) dm(x) - (integral_X h(x) dm(x)) log(integral_X h(x) dm(x)). Every integral is a real Bochner integral over all X, not an extended-real integral; log(0) = 0. Lean totalizes the Bochner integral by assigning zero when integrability fails. P(m,G,D,c) means: for every f : X -> R, D(f), Integrable(f^2,m), Integrable(f^2 log(f^2),m), Integrable(G(f),m), and G(f) >= 0 m-almost everywhere imply Ent_m(f^2) <= 2 c integral_X G(f)(x) dm(x). G and D are fixed outside the test quantifier. This does not assert that every D-test has the stated integrability or sign. P is vacuous if no test satisfies every antecedent, including if D is empty. There is no implicit topology, smoothness, derivative, or structural condition on G. Explicitly, every admissible f whose f^2, f^2 log(f^2), and Gamma(f) are nu-integrable and whose Gamma(f) is nonnegative nu-almost everywhere satisfies Ent_nu(f^2) <= 2 [C exp(u-l)] integral_X Gamma(f) dnu. No separate exponential-integrability or positive-normalization premise is displayed: almost-everywhere measurability and finite real bounds under a probability law imply exp(l) <= Z <= exp(u), hence positive finite normalization.
objects: X, probability measure mu, fixed Gamma and admissible, real C,l,u, almost-everywhere measurable B, real normalizer Z, tilted measure nu, and all qualifying real tests f.
domains: X is any measurable space; B,f : X -> R; Gamma : (X -> R) -> (X -> R); admissible : (X -> R) -> Prop. C,l,u are finite reals and C is nonnegative. Z, entropy, and energy integrals are real over X. The density for withDensity has nonnegative extended-real values through ofReal.
quantifiers: For all X, mu, Gamma, admissible, C,l,u,B, the stated assumptions imply the target predicate for every f : X -> R with target-specific premises. Each bound on B is mu-almost everywhere. The same Gamma and admissible stay fixed across both measures and all tests.
assumptions: mu has mass one; C >= 0; B is AEMeasurable under mu; l <= B mu-almost everywhere; B <= u mu-almost everywhere. For every f, admissible(f), mu-integrability of f^2, f^2 log(f^2), Gamma(f), and mu-almost-everywhere nonnegativity of Gamma(f) imply Ent_mu(f^2) <= 2 C integral_X Gamma(f) dmu. There is no separate exp(B)-integrability or Z > 0 premise; these follow from the finite bounds and measurability.
conclusion: For nu = mu.withDensity(x -> ofReal(exp(B(x))/(integral_X exp(B(y)) dmu(y)))), every admissible f whose f^2, f^2 log(f^2), Gamma(f) are nu-integrable and whose Gamma(f) is nonnegative nu-almost everywhere satisfies Ent_nu(f^2) <= 2 [C exp(u-l)] integral_X Gamma(f)(x) dnu(x). Ent is the real-integral formula expanded in reconstructed_theorem_text.
scopes: Bounds and measurability of B, and source test conditions, use mu. Target test conditions use the tilted nu. Bounds on B are almost everywhere, not pointwise. The normalizer is the single real integral over all X. Neither source nor target claims that all admissible tests have the required integrability or sign; either conditional predicate may be vacuous. No derivative or smoothness interpretation is required for Gamma. Entropy is real-valued, not extended-real, with log(0) = 0.
constant_dependencies: The target constant is exactly C exp(u-l), uniform over qualifying tests. It depends on the supplied source C and supplied finite bounds l,u, with B entering this factor only through those bounds. No sharpness or further constant is asserted.
